title: The Water Cycle
description: Grade 3 Science: the water cycle explained — evaporation, condensation, clouds, precipitation and collection. Label the diagram, order the cycle and do a jar experiment.

topics.title: Water Is Everywhere
topics.concept:
Water is found all around us — in seas, rivers, lakes, ponds, rain and even in the air as invisible vapour. Our bodies are mostly water too!

But here is the surprise: almost all of Earth's water is salty sea water that we cannot drink. Only a tiny part is fresh water we can use. That is why every drop is precious.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="150" fill="#e6f7ff"/><text x="55" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🌊</text><text x="55" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Seas</text><text x="165" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🏞️</text><text x="165" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Rivers</text><text x="275" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🌧️</text><text x="275" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Rain</text><text x="165" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Water is all around us</text></svg>
recap: Water is found in seas, rivers, rain, air and our bodies.
Most of Earth's water is salty and cannot be drunk.
Only a little is fresh water — so we must not waste it.

wonder.text: Most of our Earth is covered in water, yet we must never waste it. How can both be true?

qa.q: If there is so much water, why save it?
qa.a: Most of Earth's water is salty sea water we cannot drink. Only a small amount is clean, fresh water — so we must use it carefully and never waste it.
Yes! More than half of your body is water. That is why you feel thirsty and must drink water every day to stay healthy.

topics.title: Evaporation
topics.concept:
Evaporation is when the Sun's heat changes liquid water into an invisible gas called water vapour, which rises up into the air.

  • ☀️ The Sun warms the water in seas, rivers and puddles.
  • 💨 The water slowly turns into vapour and floats up.
  • This is how a wet floor or wet clothes dry up.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="160" fill="#eef9ff"/><rect y="120" width="300" height="40" fill="#5bb6f5"/><circle cx="240" cy="40" r="22" fill="#FFC93C"/><defs><marker id="ev" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#2BCB8B"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#2BCB8B" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ev)"><line x1="90" y1="118" x2="90" y2="60"/><line x1="140" y1="118" x2="140" y2="50"/><line x1="190" y1="118" x2="190" y2="60"/></g><text x="150" y="150" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#16a06a" text-anchor="middle">Evaporation — water rises as vapour</text></svg>
recap: Evaporation: the Sun turns liquid water into water vapour.
Water vapour is an invisible gas that rises into the air.

wonder.text: Leave a wet handkerchief in the sun and it dries. Where did the water go?

qa.q: Why do clothes dry faster on a sunny, windy day?
qa.a: More heat from the Sun and moving air both speed up evaporation. So wet clothes turn to vapour and dry much faster on a hot, breezy day.
No — water vapour is an invisible gas. We only see water again when the vapour cools high up and turns into tiny drops that form clouds.

topics.title: Condensation and Clouds
topics.concept:
Condensation is the opposite of evaporation: when water vapour cools down, it turns back into tiny liquid drops.

  • ☁️ High in the sky the air is cold, so vapour condenses into millions of tiny water drops — these make a cloud.
  • 🥤 On a cold glass, vapour in the air condenses into drops on the outside.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="160" fill="#eef9ff"/><g fill="#fff" stroke="#cfe3ff" stroke-width="2"><ellipse cx="120" cy="60" rx="48" ry="24"/><ellipse cx="96" cy="72" rx="30" ry="18"/><ellipse cx="146" cy="72" rx="30" ry="18"/></g><text x="235" y="90" font-size="36" text-anchor="middle">🥤</text><g fill="#9fd0ff"><circle cx="258" cy="80" r="3"/><circle cx="262" cy="95" r="3"/></g><text x="150" y="145" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#1f7fe0" text-anchor="middle">Condensation — vapour cools into drops</text></svg>
recap: Condensation: cooling vapour turns back into water drops.
Clouds are millions of tiny water drops in the sky.
Drops on a cold glass are condensation.

wonder.text: Why do tiny water drops appear on the outside of a cold glass of juice?

qa.q: So a cloud is made of water?
qa.a: Yes! A cloud is millions of tiny water drops (and sometimes ice crystals) floating together. When they join into bigger drops, it can rain.

qa.q: Why does the cold glass get wet outside?
qa.a: Warm air around the glass touches the cold surface and cools down. Its water vapour condenses into little drops on the glass — that is condensation!

topics.title: Precipitation: Rain and Snow
topics.concept:
Precipitation is when water falls from the clouds back to the ground.

  • 🌧️ The tiny drops in a cloud join into bigger, heavier drops.
  • When they are too heavy to float, they fall as rain.
  • ❄️ In very cold places, the water freezes and falls as snow or hail.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="160" fill="#eef9ff"/><g fill="#cfd8e6" stroke="#9fb0c8" stroke-width="2"><ellipse cx="150" cy="50" rx="56" ry="26"/><ellipse cx="120" cy="64" rx="34" ry="18"/><ellipse cx="180" cy="64" rx="34" ry="18"/></g><g stroke="#3CA7FF" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"><line x1="120" y1="88" x2="114" y2="118"/><line x1="150" y1="88" x2="146" y2="124"/><line x1="180" y1="88" x2="186" y2="118"/></g><text x="150" y="150" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#1f7fe0" text-anchor="middle">Precipitation — rain or snow falls</text></svg>
recap: Precipitation: water falls from clouds to the ground.
Warm air → rain; very cold air → snow or hail.
Drops fall when they become too heavy to float.

wonder.text: Clouds hold tiny drops. What makes those drops finally fall to the ground?

qa.q: Why does it rain and not always snow?
qa.a: If the air is warm, the water falls as liquid rain. Only when the air is very cold does the water freeze and fall as snow or hail.
Hail is small balls of ice that fall from storm clouds. The water drops freeze in the cold high air and drop down as hard, icy pellets.

topics.title: The Never-Ending Cycle
topics.concept:
The water cycle is the never-ending journey of water around our Earth. It has four steps that repeat again and again:

  • ☀️ Evaporation — the Sun turns water into vapour.
  • ☁️ Condensation — vapour cools into cloud drops.
  • 🌧️ Precipitation — water falls as rain or snow.
  • 🌊 Collection — water gathers in seas, rivers and the ground… and then it all begins again!
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 360 240" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="The water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection"><rect width="360" height="240" fill="#eaf7ff"/><rect y="195" width="360" height="45" fill="#5bb6f5"/><circle cx="318" cy="40" r="26" fill="#FFC93C"/><g fill="#fff" stroke="#cfe3ff" stroke-width="2"><ellipse cx="125" cy="60" rx="52" ry="26"/><ellipse cx="98" cy="73" rx="34" ry="20"/><ellipse cx="155" cy="73" rx="34" ry="20"/></g><path d="M66 190 C64 140 78 108 100 94" stroke="#2BCB8B" stroke-width="4" fill="none" marker-end="url(#wc3)"/><defs><marker id="wc3" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L8 4 L0 8 z" fill="#2BCB8B"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#3CA7FF" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"><line x1="102" y1="100" x2="97" y2="152"/><line x1="128" y1="100" x2="126" y2="160"/><line x1="154" y1="100" x2="157" y2="152"/></g><g font-family="sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="700"><text x="125" y="50" text-anchor="middle" fill="#5b7fa6">Condensation</text><text x="128" y="182" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1f7fe0">Precipitation</text><text x="40" y="120" text-anchor="middle" fill="#16a06a">Evaporation</text><text x="285" y="214" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1c5a86">Collection</text></g></svg>
recap: The water cycle: evaporation → condensation → precipitation → collection.
Then it repeats, again and again, forever.
The same water is used over and over around Earth.

wonder.text: The rain that fell today might have been in the sea last week. How does water keep going round and round?

qa.q: Does the water cycle ever stop?
qa.a: No — it never stops! Water keeps moving from the sea to the sky and back again, day and night, all year round. It is one of nature's greatest wonders.

qa.q: Is the water we drink today old?
qa.a: Very old! The same water has cycled around Earth for millions of years. The water in your glass may once have been a cloud, a river, or even rain a dinosaur drank!

questions.explanation: Evaporation is the Sun turning liquid water into water vapour.
Clouds are millions of tiny water drops.

questions.q: When water falls from clouds as rain, it is called…
questions.explanation: Precipitation is water falling from clouds as rain, snow or hail.
Most of Earth's water is salty sea water we cannot drink.

questions.q: Drops on the outside of a cold glass form by…
questions.explanation: Warm vapour cools on the cold glass and condenses into drops.
The water cycle repeats again and again, never stopping.

questions.q: Why do wet clothes dry faster on a hot, windy day?
options: Heat and moving air both speed up evaporation
questions.explanation: More heat and moving air make water evaporate faster, so clothes dry quicker.
Evaporation turns water to vapour; condensation turns vapour back to water.

questions.q: Why does it snow instead of rain in very cold places?
options: The water freezes in the very cold air
questions.explanation: When the air is very cold, the falling water freezes into snow or hail.

questions.q: Put the water cycle in order, starting with the Sun's heat.
questions.explanation: Evaporation → condensation → precipitation → collection, then repeat.

questions.q: Why is the water we drink millions of years old?
options: The same water keeps cycling around Earth over and over
questions.explanation: The same water keeps moving through the water cycle for millions of years.
